[b]The Horse part 2[/b]

The horse in question, was not really a horse, but more of a pony with a crown, standing at half the height of an average man, the equine who had come to see the Emperor of Elesyr was none other than the Archprince of Equestria, Wenceslaus Slazač IV, a near absolute prince from the Principate of Equestria, a country that sat to the north of Thýven and across imperial borders, that had a special arrangement with Thýven dating back centuries. It was a begrudging matter to Erjk Drs, but he nevertheless decided to meet with the archprince as a courtesy.

Strolling into the grand salon, where all guests were to be met, the archprince was standing admiring a fine painting depicting a battle that had happened centuries prior between two groups Erjk couldnt remember. 

Ah, yes, the battle of lousáne, began Erjk as he strolled into the room, his hastily put on silk robes flowing about him.

A victory I heard, replied Wenceslaus, turning to Erjk, telling that Erjk knew nothing of what he had just said.

Yes, yes, replied Erjk, waving his hand as he stopped in the middle of the room, Now, what can I do for you archprince? he enquired in a tone that betrayed his slight annoyance at being interrupted.

Word has arrived that you have crowned yourself Emperor of Elesyr and united with Vespurias in a formal union, replied the archprince.

And what has that to do with you? enquired Erjk, his annoyance coming through further.

It has much to do with us your majesty, the ascension to emperorship tips the scales that we have had balanced since the 16th century, we are a principate, and you are a kingdom, we have obligations of fee to you, and that is how it has always been, replied Wenceslaus. 

Yes, and the agreement doesnt change with my ascension, replied Erjk.

But does it? replied Wenceslaus, See, by becoming emperor, you have set off the members of the House of Lords Temporal into wondering why the princes have not sought to ascend to the kingship, making Equestria a formal kingdom, he stated, moving towards the window, However, they do not knowor perhaps they intend merely to annoy me, that if we become a kingdom, it would break the deal that weve had, he continued.

So you seek to be free from the deal? To become kings? enquired Erjk, wondering where Wenceslaus was going with his little monologue. 

No, I want a guarantee of protection, I want to ensure that we remain the same as we have always been, no expansion, no moves of annexation, and so on, he replied. 

Then you have it, replied Erjk, waving his hand, You have it!.

Good, I am glad to hear this, replied Wenceslaus, bowing, Well then, I apologise for bothering you, I shall be on my way, he continued, walking out of the room

[b]A Narrow Path | Erene2000 | Second Flouesch Republic[/b] 

"Brothers! Sisters! Friends of our Revolution..."

[i]Said the young and ethunastic Emily Schiltz, a commander within the National Republican Army on top of a freshly toppled statue out front of the Téiernsbuer City Hall to a cheering crowd of thousands[/i]

"Stand with me now! Today in this square, we will light a torch that will burn the whole world!

 No longer will the people of Floueschia suffer under the tyranny of the oligarch class! No longer will we turn over our power and the fruits of labor to the noble houses! No longer shall laws made for our benefit be shot down by an out-of-touch House of Lords! No longer shall Floueschians be sent to die in foreign wars to line the noble's pockets, no longer shall lions be led by donkeys! Floueschia belongs to her people now. Together now, we build a republic for all of us, a more just form of governance. The blood of the tyrants that is floating across the waters of the tyrant's pool shall set an example to all tyrants what their fate shall be in the coming decades, they will receive nothing but the noose and the bullet!. Our new republic will stand as a shining example to the workers and common men of the world of what can be built if they simply realize what we did! That they have nothing, NOTHING to lose but their chains. Long live the Revolution! Long Live Floueschia! 

[b]Sic Semper Tyrannis![/b]"

______________________________________________________________________________________

[Spoiler=Lamentations (Exiles)]
"..."

[i]Prince Maximilien, the now orphaned, defeated, embarrassed, and alone crown prince, if such a title even meant anything anymore, who had been only days earlier smuggled out of the besieged city of velvetel with his younger sister and older brother in a crowded cargo car of a semi truck disguised as an aid convoy to the city of Kommend. Laid on top of the cockpit of VAAB-37B stationed on the deck of the RNS Moselle, a helicarrier that had been crowded with whatever equipment the royalists could smuggle out of the country. It was the middle of the night, and therefore all of the ships surrounding the helicarrier, including its own lights, were off to avoid detection from roaming republican air sorties. Already, the Royal Navy had lost a destroyer and cruiser to ambushes in the middle of the night. and he simply looked into the deep night sky. He would think about how even he ended up in this situation. Before the revolution, he lived like a true king; he had no worries of becoming king, that was for his brother, he could simply enjoy the luxury and fame that being a prince had gotten him, now, he slept in the cold and soulless bunks of an old, rotting carrier, with no destination or hope of rescue yet, his brother so horrified by velvet that he had renounced the throne forever.

How. How could any of this have happened? He never noticed anything wrong as a child; they were always welcomed by adoring crowds everywhere they went. Was it all fake? Were the people who smiled at him when he waved at them just faking it all? It all happened so fast, he was alarmed when he overheard his parents talking about "militas" and "gurellias" but his brother always assured him they were a minority, a non-issue. Now on the television set, he was granted all he could see is celebration across the nation, statues of his parents and ancestors torn down, velvet in flames from fires started by the revolutionaries, an entire city left to burn...Almost a hundred executed, including his parents on the foots of the palace he spent his entire life in. An- [/i]

"Your Highness..." [i]Said one of the sailors, who had walked on the deck a couple minutes ago and was lingering in the corner of his eye[/i]

"Yes?" [i]He responded, surprised.[/i]

"The radio operators have a diplomat from Thýven on the line, Admiral Vivan just negotiated an agreement with them."

"That being...?"

"They are willing to take us in."

[i]Wide eyed he looked at the sailor again and asked him to confirm, for the first time in nearly a week, he felt... at least if not hopeful, at least secure that he would survive this.[/i]

[/Spoiler]

[b][sub]Be careful what you wish for...[/sub][/b]
[spoiler=be careful what you wish for...I]
[i]Three weeks after the fall of velvetel, the revolutionaries who had so long wished for a republic to replace their decadent monarchy, a republic that would be for all of them. Had succeeded, the monarchists were now utterly broken, their leaders were now lying face down in the reflecting pool that was the pinnacle of their decadence. Or rotting on nooses on the steps of the palace that they once hid in, if there was ever a problem that required the military to put down yet another group of strikers. 12 years since the delegation of 100 members of the House of Commons stormed out, 6 years of revolution, and it had finally all come crumbling down. But this "Second Republic" was not in any better of a situation. Even in victory, the military, which had long been a disorganized band of mercenaries, fools, dreamers, criminals, and thugs, and the government were on uneven footing, and were now struggling to establish order in their new, vastly overstrained administration. The entire civil service had practically collapsed, with most members of it fearing they would be tried with collaboration and put to death, fleeing the country or going into hiding, slipping back into flourishing society as the government was unable to enforce any of its new laws. Crime was rampant, and many took victory as cause to begin looting, especially former government offices and the hundreds of royal buildings across various cities. And with no police force to restore order, policing was forced to be a task given to the military, and with it equally radicalized at this point, most soldiers could not and did not bother to actually enforce law and order.

Many across the nation began taking out their grievances against the human minority of the nation, who had long been seen as above the Nronesch Majority due to their prominent position within the monarchist order and being one of the richest groups of the nation. Many humans were unwilling to take this lying down, and being just as well armed, and many being former royalist soldiers, began to take up arms, now adding ethnic violence to the ever-growing pile of problems. For Friedrich Müller, becoming consul of the nation had turned from a dream; he proudly accepted the nomination after all, but now, it was nothing but a nightmare, and the violence and chaos occurring across the new republic was a bitter awakening that a revolution based on violence would only create a country of violence. He had to do something, but then another issue turned its ugly head. The monarchy had kept the economy stable through its vast gold reserves, the navy had taken these gold reserves with them, meaning that effectively, the Flouesch Assignat was now practically worthless, with inflation exploding due to the collapse of the economy within the weeks many would lose there jobs and become homeless as the government had to instiute an emergency rent freeze, with now thousands on the streets Müller could only watch as, just like the nation, the economy burned down. Muller had a decision to make: he could rebuild the government or the economy. He decided the government would, at the very least, grant the new republic more legitimacy among the populace.

He started by announcing that the Republic Constitution that had been drafted by the delegation of 100 would become the new constitution of the fledgling Republic, canceling the Revolutionary Council of State's initial plans to draft an entirely new one. He stated that he had to do this, using his emergency authority as caretaker to ensure a far smoother transition from monarchy to republic than had been attempted thus far, and that this constitution would only become an "Interim Constitution" until the situation in the country had stabilized. Begrudgingly, the Revolutionary Council just barely accepted the problem. The problem Muller was facing now, in fact, the biggest problem outside of the collapse of most of the civil service, was that the Republic's wartime coalition. The National Revolutionary Republican Council, or the NRRC had collapsed. Differences between its two primary factions, the Moderate Socialists, the Jacobins, and the Social Liberals were simply far, far too great to reconcile. These two factions had quickly reconstituted them into three new parties, the Social Republican Federation, the Radical Republican Party, and the National Democratic Alliance. Anyone who fell outside of these factions fell into the Union of Liberal Republicans, People's Rally, and The Left. With now 6 new parties in government, many were calling for actual elections to be held. And thus, Friedrich Müller,using his emergency authority as caretaker, declared that the interim government would disband itself starting on July 30th, and called a National Election...[/i][/spoiler]

[spoiler=be careful what you wish for II]
[i] Friedrich Müller was surprised when he saw the results, to say the least. He had run, thinking that he couldn't possibly actually beat the legendary reputation of Emily Schilitz, and believing that the chaos that the republic had endured under his caretakership would only tank his reputation. But unknowingly to him he was beloved by the people, many saw him, not Schiltz as the Father of their republic, he won in a landslide. In his speech, he accepted the position of first consul with grace, declaring that while he would retain emergency powers as the Staatsrot requested of him. He would govern the nation with thoughtfulness and moderation. He would not pick sides, and he hoped to guide the republic through its troubles, whatever that would entail. He declared that the path the republic faced was a narrow and dangerous one, but that it was them, the people, who moved history. His first matter of business as consul was making sure the Revolutionary Council of State formed a government. No party had gained a majority as expected, so using his influence in the SRF he convinced them to form a coalition with the second largest party, the RRP. The SRF was the bulk of the Moderate Socialist and Revolutionaries, so working with the RRP would be difficult. Negotiations included concessions from both sides; the SRF would not attempt to force the RRP into canceling the "Legal Purge" and it would continue in a limited fashion. While the RRP would not be able to totally eliminate the capitalist system, instead, both parties would work towards forging a more humanistic form of capitalism across the nation. Additionally. Emily Schiltz, leader of the RRP would be given the First Tribune and allowed to form the government so long as she appointed members from both parties. 

Additionally, the SRF got the Presidency of the Staatssrot. Deciding to establish some sort of voice for the opposition, Friedrich Müller demanded during the negotiations that both parties agree to appoint a member to the Vice Presidency of the Staatsrot. Lastly was revolving around the military, the Ministry of the Interior, which would be controlled by the RRP would get their "Internal Revolutionary Guard" while the SRF would get their campaign promise of demobilization for the General Army. Now that a government had been formed. Friedrich Müller would start slowly rebuilding the civil service. By announcing a general pardon of all civil servants who had evidence of significant evidence of "Collaboration" with royalist authorities, so long as they accepted 2 conditions. A dock in their pay for 6 months, and returning to work within 5 months of the proclamation. To assist with this, he established, with the permission of the Staatsrot, the "Advisory Board on Clemency for Civil Servants." Meanwhile, the legal purge would begin in force. Starting with the royalist military, who had been captured. The trials in these purges would be much more organized. In all, around 3,000 royalist military personnel would be charged with war crimes, treason, and tyranny within the coming months. 120 of these would be given life sentences, and around 500 would be given house arrest. While the remainder would be either put to death or forced to take a lowering in rank in the NVA, followed by a dishonorable discharge from it.

Speaking of the NVA. Part of rebuilding the government would inherently mean reducing its power it held within it. Firstly, Muller announced that he was dismissing several of its generals, accusing them of attempting to establish a military dictatorship with how forceful they were acting towards the civilian government. This wasn't wrong as The Republican Security Services the next day after raiding and searching their former offices, found plans of a coup attempt to remove Mueller and put themselves in charge, at least, that's what they claimed. Muller had the RSS secretly make the evidence up. While he hated to do this, lying to protect the republic was better than letting the military potentially destroy it from within. The public scandal enabled further crackdowns against the military, with the State Security Law being drafted and passed through the staatrot, amending the new constitution, stating simply that the military was to remain politically neutral and subservient to the civilian government and the wider public. This included an elected officer corps and allowed collective bargaining among soldier unions in the military. Amazingly, the old constitution included provisions for this not to be the case, although it was likely a holdover from the old royalist constitution. As the month of September came to the close, now almost 3 months on from the revolution. Muller would take to his balcony overlooking Téiernsbuer. Whine in hand. Rebuilding the country was going to be no easy feat, but at least for now, he could rest a little bit easier. Leaving his office he went down to the staatrots chamber, where they had just finally adopted a national anthem for the new republic, the entire chamber erupted in song...[/i][/spoiler]
